missions.title: Install the RAM
missions.description: Practice: slide a RAM stick into its slot. Learn to grab, carry and drop parts.
intro: Drag the RAM stick into the RAM slot.
success: RAM installed! Memory holds what the CPU is working on right now.

Motherboard/RamSlot.name: RAM slot
Motherboard/RamSlot.hint: The long slot is for memory (RAM): it holds what the CPU is working on right now.

missions.title: Identify the components
missions.description: Find the CPU, memory, storage and input/output parts and put each where it belongs.
intro: Every computer needs four things: a processor, memory, storage, and a way to talk to people.
Put each part on the table where it belongs. Pick up any part to start.
success: You built the core of a computer: processor, memory, storage and input.

Motherboard/CpuSocket.name: CPU socket
Motherboard/CpuSocket.hint: The square socket is for the processor (CPU): it runs every instruction.

Motherboard/RamSlot.name: RAM slot
Motherboard/RamSlot.hint: The long slot is for memory (RAM): it holds what the CPU is working on right now.

Motherboard/M2Slot.name: M.2 storage slot
Motherboard/M2Slot.hint: The flat M.2 slot is for storage (the SSD): it keeps files and programs even when the power is off.

UsbPad.name: keyboard spot (USB port)
UsbPad.hint: The USB spot is for input and output devices: the keyboard is how a person gives the computer input.

missions.title: Assemble the system
missions.description: Build a working computer from its parts, in the order that makes it run.
intro: Build the computer inside its case. Every part has a job.
Mount the motherboard, the power supply (PSU) and the SSD. Plug the power in last.
success: The computer is assembled: the PSU powers everything, the motherboard connects it, and the SSD stores it.

MotherboardTray.name: motherboard tray
MotherboardTray.hint: The big tray is for the motherboard: the board every other part plugs into.
MotherboardTray.role: The motherboard connects every part so they can send data to each other.

PsuBay.name: PSU bay
PsuBay.hint: The bay by the back is for the power supply (PSU).
PsuBay.role: The PSU turns wall power into the steady voltages every part needs.

DriveBay.name: drive bay
DriveBay.hint: The small bay is for storage: the SSD keeps files when the power is off.
DriveBay.role: The SSD stores the operating system, programs and files.

PowerSocket.name: power socket
PowerSocket.hint: Power goes in last, once every part is mounted, so nothing is live while you build.
PowerSocket.role: Power is connected. The computer can start.

missions.title: Execute a task
missions.description: Follow a task as its data moves from storage, to memory, to the CPU.
intro: Open a photo. The photo file (the glowing cube) starts on the SSD.
Carry it the way data really moves: into memory, through the processor, and onto the screen.
success: That's how every program runs: storage to memory, memory to the CPU, and the result to an output device.

MemoryStage.name: memory (RAM)
MemoryStage.hint: Programs and files are loaded into memory first, because the CPU can only work with what's in RAM.
MemoryStage.role: The photo is copied from storage into memory (RAM), where the CPU can reach it fast.

CpuStage.name: processor (CPU)
CpuStage.hint: The CPU reads its data from memory, so the photo has to be in RAM before the CPU can decode it.
CpuStage.role: The CPU follows the program's instructions to decode the photo into pixels.

ScreenStage.name: screen
ScreenStage.hint: The screen shows what the CPU has finished, so the photo has to be processed first.
ScreenStage.role: The pixels are sent to the screen, an output device.

missions.title: Add processing capacity
missions.description: Add a graphics card and see which jobs run faster on a GPU than a CPU.
intro: Some jobs are a long list of steps. Others repeat the same math millions of times.
Install the graphics card (GPU), then send each job to the processor that's best at it: the CPU or the GPU.
success: CPUs have a few fast cores for step-by-step work. GPUs have thousands of small cores that run the same math at the same time: that's parallel computing.

GpuSlot.name: graphics card slot
GpuSlot.hint: The long slot under the board's middle is for the graphics card (GPU).
GpuSlot.role: The GPU adds thousands of small cores for work that can be split up.

CpuJobs.name: CPU jobs
CpuJobs.hint: The CPU has a few very fast cores. It's best at jobs where each step depends on the last, like following a game's rules or checking a password.
CpuJobs.role: Step-by-step work goes to the CPU: each step needs the one before it.

GpuJobs.name: GPU jobs
GpuJobs.hint: The GPU does the same math on many pieces at once. It's best at jobs that split into millions of identical parts, like coloring pixels or training an AI model.
GpuJobs.role: Work that splits into many identical pieces goes to the GPU, all at the same time.

missions.title: Diagnose a failure
missions.description: A computer won't work. Find the faulty parts and replace them.
intro: This computer won't start properly: when it turns on, it beeps and shows no picture.
Find the broken part and swap in the right spare from the table. Drop the spare on the part you think is broken.
success: Fixed! Bad memory failed the start-up test, and a dead drive hid the operating system. Each part fails in its own way, which is how you can tell them apart.

RamProblem.name: Problem 1: beeps, no picture
RamProblem.hint: Beeping with no picture is the start-up memory test failing: nothing can run without working RAM.
RamProblem.role: The new RAM passes the memory test. The computer starts... but now the screen says "No boot device found".

DriveProblem.name: Problem 2: "No boot device found"
DriveProblem.hint: "No boot device" means the computer can't find the drive that holds the operating system: that's storage.

CpuCheck.name: CPU
CpuCheck.hint: The CPU is fine: a dead CPU usually means no beeps at all, because nothing can run the start-up test.

PsuCheck.name: power supply
PsuCheck.hint: The power supply is fine: the computer turns on and beeps, so it's getting power.

missions.title: Build your own PC
missions.description: Pick parts from three tiers and build a PC that works.
intro: Pick a motherboard first: its socket and slots decide which parts fit.
Then add a CPU, memory, storage, a graphics card and a power supply from any row, and press the power button with the finger.
success: It boots! Every part in this PC works with the others.
boot_lines: POST: checking CPU, memory, storage... OK

Case/BoardTray.name: motherboard tray
Case/BoardTray.hint: This tray holds the motherboard. Every other part has its own place on the board or beside it.
Case/BoardTray.role: The motherboard joins every part together. Its socket and slots decide what fits.

Case/CpuSocket.name: CPU socket
Case/CpuSocket.hint: The socket takes the processor (CPU): it runs every instruction.
Case/CpuSocket.role: The CPU runs every instruction. Its socket has to match the motherboard's.

Case/RamSlots.name: memory slots
Case/RamSlots.hint: The long slots take memory (RAM): it holds what the CPU is working on right now.
Case/RamSlots.role: Memory holds what the CPU is working on right now.

Case/StorageBay.name: storage slot
Case/StorageBay.hint: Storage goes here: it keeps your files when the power is off.
Case/StorageBay.role: Storage keeps the operating system and your files when the power is off.

Case/GpuSlot.name: graphics card slot
Case/GpuSlot.hint: The long slot takes the graphics card: it makes the picture.
Case/GpuSlot.role: The graphics card makes the picture. A big one needs its own power cable.

Case/PsuBay.name: power supply bay
Case/PsuBay.hint: The power supply goes here: it feeds every part.
Case/PsuBay.role: The power supply feeds every part, so it has to be big enough for all of them.

Case/PowerButton.name: power button
Case/PowerButton.hint: Press the power button with the finger once every part is in.

missions.title: Unbox the PC
missions.description: Lift the tower, monitor, keyboard and mouse out of the box and set each one on the desk.
intro: A new PC comes as four things: the tower, a monitor, a keyboard and a mouse.
Lift each one out of the box and put it on its marked spot on the desk.
success: Unboxed! The tower does the computing, the monitor shows the output, and the keyboard and mouse are how you give it input.

Desk/TowerSpot.name: tower spot
Desk/TowerSpot.hint: This spot is for the tower, the big case the other parts plug into.
Desk/TowerSpot.role: The tower is the computer itself: the processor, memory and storage are inside it.

Desk/MonitorSpot.name: monitor spot
Desk/MonitorSpot.hint: This spot is for the monitor, the screen you look at.
Desk/MonitorSpot.role: The monitor is an output device: it shows you what the computer is doing.

Desk/KeyboardSpot.name: keyboard spot
Desk/KeyboardSpot.hint: This spot is for the keyboard, the one you type on.
Desk/KeyboardSpot.role: The keyboard is an input device: it sends what you type into the computer.

Desk/MouseSpot.name: mouse spot
Desk/MouseSpot.hint: This spot is for the mouse, the one you point and click with.
Desk/MouseSpot.role: The mouse is an input device: it sends your moves and clicks into the computer.

missions.title: Connect the monitor, keyboard and mouse
missions.description: Run an HDMI cable from the PC to the monitor, and plug the keyboard and mouse into USB ports.
intro: The tower is turned round so you can reach the ports on its back.
Plug the HDMI cable into the tower and the monitor, then plug the keyboard and the mouse into the USB ports.
success: Connected! HDMI carries the picture out to the monitor, and USB brings your typing and clicks in.

Tower/GpuHdmi.name: graphics card HDMI port
Tower/GpuHdmi.hint: The picture comes from the graphics card's port, the one lower down on the back.
Tower/GpuHdmi.role: The graphics card makes the picture and sends it out through this port.

Monitor/HdmiIn.name: monitor HDMI port
Monitor/HdmiIn.hint: The monitor's HDMI port takes the picture that comes from the computer.
Monitor/HdmiIn.role: The picture comes into the monitor here, so the monitor is an output device.

Tower/Usb1.name: first USB port
Tower/Usb1.hint: Keyboard and mouse are input devices: they send information into the computer.
Tower/Usb1.role: This cable carries input into the computer: every key press and click goes down it.

Tower/Usb2.name: second USB port
Tower/Usb2.hint: Keyboard and mouse are input devices: they send information into the computer.
Tower/Usb2.role: This cable carries input into the computer: every key press and click goes down it.

missions.title: Plug in power and watch it boot
missions.description: Give the tower and the monitor power, plug into the wall last, and watch the PC start up.
intro: Everything is connected except power.
Plug a power cable into the tower and one into the monitor. Then plug both into the wall: the wall always comes last.
success: It boots! First the PC tests its own hardware (POST), then the BIOS finds the drive, then the operating system loads from storage into memory.
boot_lines: POST: checking CPU, memory, storage... OK

Tower/PowerIn.name: power socket on the tower
Tower/PowerIn.hint: A power plug goes in here, on the power supply at the bottom of the tower's back.
Tower/PowerIn.role: The power supply turns wall power into the low voltages the parts inside the tower use.

Monitor/PowerIn.name: power socket on the monitor
Monitor/PowerIn.hint: A power plug goes in here. The monitor needs power of its own.
Monitor/PowerIn.role: The monitor has its own power: the HDMI cable carries the picture, not power.

Wall/Socket.name: wall socket
Wall/Socket.hint: Always plug into the wall last, after everything else is connected.
Wall/Socket.role: Power now flows from the wall to that device.

missions.title: Connect to the network
missions.description: Run an Ethernet cable from the PC to the router and watch the link light come on.
intro: The PC works, but it can't reach any other computer yet.
Plug one end of the Ethernet cable into the tower and the other into the router.
success: You're online! The cable links the PC to the router, and the router passes its messages on to other networks.

linked: This PC is on the network.

Tower/Ethernet.name: tower network port
Tower/Ethernet.hint: The network (LAN) port is the square one beside the USB ports.
Tower/Ethernet.role: The network port is how the PC sends and receives data over a cable.

Router/Lan1.name: router LAN port
Router/Lan1.hint: The router connects your computer to other networks, including the internet.
Router/Lan1.role: The router connects your computer to other networks, including the internet.

missions.title: Connect two computers
missions.description: Join two PCs with one Cat6 cable: the smallest network there is.
intro: Two PCs on a desk can't share anything yet.
Plug one end of the blue Cat6 cable into PC A's LAN port and the other end into PC B's.
success: That's a network! Two devices joined by a cable can share data.
A cable between two computers is the smallest network: two devices that can share data.

PcA/Eth0.name: PC A LAN port
PcA/Eth0.hint: A cable between two computers is the smallest network: two devices that can share data.
PcA/Eth0.role: The LAN port is how a PC sends and receives data over a cable.

PcA/Power.name: PC A power socket
PcA/Power.hint: That's the power socket. The network cable goes in the LAN port beside it.

PcB/Eth0.name: PC B LAN port
PcB/Eth0.hint: A cable between two computers is the smallest network: two devices that can share data.
PcB/Eth0.role: The LAN port is how a PC sends and receives data over a cable.

PcB/Power.name: PC B power socket
PcB/Power.hint: That's the power socket. The network cable goes in the LAN port beside it.

missions.title: Add a switch
missions.description: Cable three PCs to a GS108 switch so they can all reach each other.
intro: One cable joins two computers. For three or more you need a switch.
Cable each PC's LAN port to any of the switch's 8 ports.
success: All three PCs are on one network now.
A switch connects many devices on the same local network and passes data only to the port it's meant for.

PcA/Eth0.name: PC A LAN port
PcA/Eth0.hint: A switch connects many devices on the same local network and passes data only to the port it's meant for.
PcA/Eth0.role: The LAN port is how a PC sends and receives data over a cable.

PcA/Power.hint: That's the power socket. The network cable goes in the LAN port beside it.

PcB/Power.hint: That's the power socket. The network cable goes in the LAN port beside it.

PcC/Eth0.name: PC C LAN port
PcC/Eth0.hint: A switch connects many devices on the same local network and passes data only to the port it's meant for.
PcC/Eth0.role: The LAN port is how a PC sends and receives data over a cable.

PcC/Power.name: PC C power socket
PcC/Power.hint: That's the power socket. The network cable goes in the LAN port beside it.

Switch/Port1.hint: A switch connects many devices on the same local network and passes data only to the port it's meant for.
Switch/Port1.role: Any free port works: the switch learns which PC is on which port.

Switch/Port8.hint: A switch connects many devices on the same local network and passes data only to the port it's meant for.
Switch/Port8.role: Any free port works: the switch learns which PC is on which port.

missions.title: Add a router
missions.description: Connect the switch to a router, and the router to the internet.
intro: The three PCs reach each other, but not the internet.
Cable the switch to one of the router's LAN ports, then the wall's Internet jack to the router's WAN port.
success: A router connects networks together. LAN is your side; WAN goes out to the internet.

PcA/Eth0.name: PC A LAN port
PcA/Eth0.hint: A router connects networks together. LAN is your side; WAN goes out to the internet.
PcA/Eth0.role: The LAN port is how a PC sends and receives data over a cable.

PcA/Power.name: PC A power socket
PcA/Power.hint: That's the power socket. The network cable goes in the LAN port beside it.

Switch/Port8.role: Any free port works: the switch learns which PC is on which port.

Router/Wan.name: Router WAN port
Router/Wan.hint: WAN goes out to the internet: only the cable from the wall's Internet jack goes here. The switch goes in a LAN port.
Router/Wan.role: The WAN port joins your network to the internet.

Router/Lan1.name: Router LAN 1 port
Router/Lan1.hint: LAN is your side: the cable from the switch goes here. The internet cable goes in WAN.
Router/Lan1.role: The LAN ports are your side of the router: your own network.

Router/Lan2.name: Router LAN 2 port
Router/Lan2.hint: LAN is your side: the cable from the switch goes here. The internet cable goes in WAN.
Router/Lan2.role: The LAN ports are your side of the router: your own network.

Jack/Jack.name: Internet Internet jack
Jack/Jack.hint: The wall's Internet jack only takes the internet cable, which goes to the router's WAN port.
Jack/Jack.role: The wall jack is where the internet comes into the room.

missions.title: Send data and watch the packets
missions.description: Send a message from PC A to PC C and watch it travel as numbered packets.
intro: The PCs are cabled to the switch. Now send something!
Drop the message card into PC A's Outbox. It's addressed to PC C.
success: Every packet arrived, and PC C put them back in order.
Data is split into packets. Each one carries the address it's going to, and they can arrive out of order.

PcA/Eth0.hint: Data is split into packets. Each one carries the address it's going to, and they can arrive out of order.
PcA/Eth0.role: The LAN port is how a PC sends and receives data over a cable.
